title: ELiDDI activities configuration
description: Validates config/config.json. `general` metadata is documented but not read by build code; `day_boundary` and `instructions` (onboarding steps) are read directly off the top level by src/ at runtime; `timeline` order controls display order in the JS-enhanced layer (see the `timeline` definition below) - scripts/generate_no_js.js itself is order-independent.

day_boundary.description: Clock time (HH:MM) that the diary day starts at - read as GLOBALS.DATA.day_boundary by src/utils/time.js and others, not by any field under general.

instructions.description: Onboarding walkthrough steps, read as GLOBALS.DATA.instructions by src/components/onboarding and src/components/contextualHelp.
Despite the name, this is a boolean toggle, not text - the actual onboarding step text lives in the top-level `instructions` array.

autoscrollSpeed.description: ELiDDI-specific extension - not part of the upstream O-TUD accessibility spec.

timeline.description: Order controls display order only, in the JS-enhanced layer: src/components/timelineStack/timelineStack.js assigns each dimension a 0-based index in array order, and that index is what Timeline/ActivityPicker use to look up GLOBALS.DATA.timeline[dimensionIndex] - so array position determines which dimension shows first and the picker's left-to-right sequence, not which dimension it must be. No dimension is required at a specific index. scripts/generate_no_js.js itself is order-independent - it builds every dimension's no-JS form generically from that dimension's own `mode`/`name` fields, never by position.

min_coverage.description: A string of digits, not a number, despite representing a numeric minimum coverage.

name.description: A literal single space (" ") is used as a dummy name on columns with no real category grouping - deliberately not restricted to non-whitespace.

activity.description: Activities come in two observed flavors: 'coded' (code/label/short/vshort, used by Primary/Secondary) and 'example' (examples, always "", used by Location/Who/Device/Enjoyment) - plus a minimal third shape (name + color only) for some 'Other' entries.
